What it is for

Six questions your board will end up asking

Almost every company has AI pilots. Very few can answer these without opening six spreadsheets. SEVEN-G is built to answer them.

01Am I moving forward with AI?How many initiatives come in, how many reach production, where they get stuck and how long they take. A funnel, as in sales. 02Are my use cases profitable?Full cost against efficiencies and return. Only validated value adds up: "freed" capacity that nobody turns into savings does not count. 03Could my company do more?Nine impact spheres and three ambition levels show where value is still unexplored, and maturity tells you whether you are ready. 04Am I transforming, or just getting more efficient?An index with eight signals tells evidenced transformation apart from the kind that only exists on a slide. 05Do I know when to stop?Eight phases with decision gates. Stopping an initiative with a recorded reason and lesson is an outcome, not a failure. 06Is risk under control?Inventory, risk matrix, segregated roles —whoever builds does not audit— and orderly evidence for whatever regulation applies to you.

Do I know when to stop? Is risk under control?

A gate before every big spend

Every initiative goes through eight phases, from idea to operation. Between phases there is a gate with five possible outcomes: continue, continue with conditions, iterate, pivot or stop.

The third one is the one that matters: feasibility and risk, before the heavy investment. And no gate is passed on results alone: it takes the objective met and the evidence that proves it.

See how an initiative flows →

Could you do more? Are you transforming?

From one-off savings to transformation you can prove

A map of nine spheres by three ambition levels —optimise, augment, transform— shows where your AI is today and where you have not looked yet.

A maturity assessment across seven dimensions tells you which step the organisation is on, from 0 —chaos or scattered proofs of concept— to 5 —optimised, with evidenced transformation—, and the transformation index separates what is proven from what is merely declared.
